about: Compiler bugs that the human has ruled on, one entry per file in compiler-bugs/, named after its decision-log id; this file lists them. Each entry has a reproducer that was run on the
pinned compiler when it was added (`reference`). The decision log (decision-log.md) holds the reasoning.
A ruling is confirmed when the human has discussed the intended semantics with Modular's
developers; the outcome goes in `confirmation`. If a ruling turns out wrong, the human
`fixed` states what the fixed compiler does, as the human ruled; the model does that.
`upstream.status`: unfiled, filed, fixed-upstream. Only the human files upstream reports.
`nightly` records the last check of the reproducer on a Mojo nightly, before the human meets Modular.

`upstream.tracking` is this project's issue that tracks the report, or the upstream issues that track the bug when others filed it. `upstream.related` lists upstream issues that probably share the bug's cause.
`compiler` says what the current pin, the nightly 1.3.0.dev2026111905 since D-0007, does with the reproducer; `reference` keeps the pin it was ruled at.

bugs.title: xs[i] = f(xs) stores into a stale element when f grows or shrinks xs
a struct initialized field by field destroys a field that was never set
@fieldwise_init fails inside a struct cycle through a List, where the hand-written initializer compiles: at the pin with the holder B declared first, on 1.2.0 in either declaration order
var x: Int = [e1, ..., en] is accepted for every n, keeps e1 when n >= 2 and crashes at run time when n = 0
a struct on a cycle through a List is rejected as non-'Deinitable', depending on which structs have a __deinit__ of their own
List[Int](range(start, end, step)) aborts when the range is not empty and start - end is ±2^63
indexing an Int ignores the index: k[1], k[-1] and k[n] read and write k with no error
two one-element arrays compare as equal in an optimized build when a struct's __deinit__ prints
an assignment whose value is the target itself destroys the old value before copying it
arrays of arrays of one-element arrays compare wrongly at -O3 when two comparisons of them are printed together
